title: Skow Island (South Oyster Bay)
summary: Skow Island is a tidal marsh island in South Oyster Bay. Tooker recorded Skow as an early-map spelling associated with the island; modern federal maps preserve the island at this exact location under an outdated historical name.
address_label: South Oyster Bay marsh island, Nassau County, NY
map_geometry_source: U.S. Geological Survey South Oyster Bay mapping and GNIS island coordinate.
why_this_matters: The island is a clearly identifiable part of the South Oyster Bay marsh landscape. Mapping it with careful language allows the archive to preserve a historical place-name record without repeating outdated terminology as an unqualified public label.
introduction_content: The island lies among the tidal marshes south of Massapequa. Its geographic identity is confirmed by modern U.S. Geological Survey mapping, while its historical name requires respectful context because the longer form used on many maps is now recognized as offensive.
history_content: Tooker repeated a refuge story involving Native women and children during conflict, but did not document the story to an earlier record. The listing therefore preserves it as a reported tradition rather than established fact.
translation_content: Tooker noted Skow as a spelling found on maps. This listing uses that shorter historical form and avoids presenting his older linguistic discussion as a modern community-approved translation.
preservation_content: This draft is retained to support source review without publishing an uncertain or harmful placename presentation.
whereintheworld_content: The marker uses the U.S. Geological Survey island coordinate in South Oyster Bay, south of Massapequa and north of the barrier beach.
